Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in the social sciences to simulate human behavior and communication, yet validation methods for these applications remain limited. Existing evaluations often rely on human judgments of plausibility, a coarse, difficult-to-scale, and often unreliable benchmark for distinguishing AI-generated from human text. As a result, researchers lack robust tools for assessing the realism of LLM-generated language and for calibrating models to real-world data. We address this gap in two ways. First, we introduce the Conversational Human Authenticity Test (CHAT), a validation framework that combines aggregate metrics of detectability and semantic similarity with interpretable linguistic features, including stylistic markers and topical patterns, to assess how closely LLMs approximate human language in a given dataset. Second, we benchmark nine open-weight LLMs across five calibration strategies, including fine-tuning, stylistic prompting, and context retrieval, on user interactions from X, Bluesky, and Reddit. We find that even after calibration, LLM outputs remain clearly distinguishable from human text, especially in affective tone and emotional expression. Instruction-tuned models generally underperform base models, and larger models do not obviously improve human-likeness. We also identify a trade-off between realism and semantic fidelity: methods that make outputs seem more human often move them further from the content of human responses. Together, these results provide a scalable framework for validation and calibration in LLM-based social simulation while underscoring current limits in reproducing human communication.
Author: Pagan, Nicolò
Source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
Title: AI-generated language remains systematically distinguishable from human communication

Abstract: Most stinging animals deliver venom by contracting muscles around a venom reservoir, but honey bees employ a fundamentally different strategy. The stingers of worker bees have the unique ability to autotomize, separating from the body, to continue to sting independently. Despite more than a century of anatomical descriptions, the mechanics of venom pumping have remained unresolved due to the challenges of observing them in action. We recorded high-speed videos of active, autotomized stingers, combined with micro computed tomography-based three-dimensional reconstruction to characterize the biomechanics of stinging in the honey bee Apis mellifera . We reveal that the stinger functions as a unique double-piston micro-pump. Two lancets, each possessing a deformable valve, slide in antiphase within a bulb chamber. These valves dynamically deform to alternately form a seal during the downstroke and collapse during the upstroke, enabling pressure generation for pumping while potentially minimizing backflow during refilling. The inverted tear-drop shape of the bulb facilitates refill even while pumping proceeds. We explored valve deformations and flow behavior by constructing a dynamically scaled physical model of the bulb chamber confirming key features of the pumping cycle and propose mechanisms for valve deformations. The double piston design adds significant design complexity but enables continuous venom delivery in a compact, autonomous unit. These findings provide deeper understanding of venom pumping in honey bees and other Hymenoptera. This study also provides evidence of an axial piston pump within a biological system and offers inspiration for the design of microfluidic pumping devices.
Author: Ramirez-Esquivel, Fiorella
Source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
Title: The honey bee stinger: An unusual pump with collapsible double pistons
Topic: Insect and Arachnid Ecology and Behavior

Abstract: Glaciers populate the mountain ranges of the western conterminous United States and despite their importance to alpine hydrology, their area and volume change have never been comprehensively evaluated. Our study shows that since the mid-twentieth century about one-quarter of the glaciers have disappeared and the overall area and volume are reduced by one-third. The pattern of glacier shrinkage suggests most glaciers in the conterminous United States are largely maintained by local topographic influences due to their small size. These results improve our understanding of evolving high alpine hydrology and importance to ecosystem processes.
Author: Andrew G. Fountain
Source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
Title: Extensive glacier loss in the coterminous United States

Abstract: Neural circuits establish a stable basal level of synaptic transmission that is maintained throughout life. When synaptic activity is perturbed, homeostatic mechanisms restore this set point, but how neurons reconcile long-term stability and rapid compensatory plasticity remains unclear. Here, we identify two competing presynaptic multimolecular complexes that control steady-state transmission and homeostatic potentiation and define the molecular switch that enables transitions between these functional states. At Drosophila neuromuscular junction, the transmembrane protein PlexinB (PlexB) and the auxiliary subunit Neto-α regulate both basal synaptic function and homeostatic plasticity. PlexB association with presynaptic KaiR1D/Neto-α receptor complexes modulates channel properties and fine-tunes neurotransmitter release, whereas PlexB signaling with Semaphorin2b (Sema2b) and Neto-α drives homeostatic potentiation. KaiR1D and Sema2b/PlexB compete for a limited pool of presynaptic Neto-α. Motor neurons switch from steady-state transmission to homeostatic potentiation by exchanging KaiR1D/Neto-α/PlexB complexes for Neto-α/PlexB/Sema2b. Critically, Neto-α must dissociate from KaiR1D-containing complexes to initiate the homeostatic response. Variants of Neto-α or KaiR1D that fail to dissociate support normal basal neurotransmission but abolish homeostatic plasticity. These findings demonstrate that dynamic reorganization of competing presynaptic protein assemblies enables neurons to preserve stable baseline transmission while mounting robust compensatory responses to perturbations. Given the widespread roles of presynaptic receptors and Semaphorin/Plexin signaling in synaptic regulation, this mechanism may represent a conserved strategy for balancing stability and plasticity in neural circuits.
Author: Hsieh, Wen-Chieh
Source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
Title: Competing presynaptic protein assemblies coordinate basal neurotransmission with homeostatic plasticity

Abstract: Chaotic dynamics, commonly seen in weather systems and fluid turbulence, are characterized by their sensitivity to initial conditions, which makes accurate prediction challenging. Recent approaches have focused on developing data-driven models that attempt to preserve invariant statistics over long horizons since many chaotic systems exhibit dissipative behaviors and ergodicity. Despite the recent progress in such models, they are still often prone to generating unbounded trajectories, leading to invalid statistics evaluation. To address this fundamental challenge, we introduce a modular framework that provides formal guarantees of trajectory boundedness for neural network chaotic dynamics models. Our core contribution is a dissipative projection layer that leverages control-theoretic principles to ensure the learned system is dissipative. Specifically, our framework simultaneously learns a dynamics emulator and an energy-like function, where the latter is used to construct an algebraic dissipative constraint within the projection layer. Furthermore, the learned invariant level set provides an outer estimate for the system’s strange attractor, which is known to be difficult to characterize due to its complex geometry. We demonstrate our model’s ability to produce bounded long-horizon forecasts that preserve invariant statistics for chaotic dynamical systems, including Lorenz 96 and a reduced-order model of the Kuramoto–Sivashinsky equation.
Author: Tang, Sunbochen
Source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
Title: Learning dissipative chaotic dynamics with boundedness guarantees

Abstract: Knowledge of how pathogens, in the context of a changing environment, shape the structure of ecological communities remains limited, and little information exists on the ability of small-scale field experiments to predict the consequences of large-scale environmental impacts. We addressed these issues using the emergence of a widespread epidemic (sea star wasting disease, SSWD) on rocky intertidal shorelines. Prior experiments demonstrated strong reductions in sessile species diversity in response to the local experimental removal of the sea star Pisaster ochraceus [R. T. Paine, Am. Nat. 100 , 65–75 (1966); R. T. Paine, Oceologia 15 , 93–120 (1974)] at our site. In surveys of sea star populations over 8 y spanning the onset of the SSWD epidemic, P. ochraceus populations declined by 90%, then subsequently recovered to about one third of pre-epidemic size under an endemic disease phase. Using four different types of temporal data, we documented large increases in populations of the competitively dominant mussel Mytilus californianus following P. ochraceus decline, which were of similar magnitude to those observed in prior field experiments. As in the field experiments, sessile species richness and diversity declined strongly following the onset of the SSWD epidemic as mussels were released from predator control. Our results reveal a strong effect of a pathogen in regulating ecological community structure by disrupting the role of a keystone species, a result anticipated by prior small-scale field experiments.
Author: John Timothy Wootton
Source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
Title: Field experiments predict ecological response to a large-scale epidemic of an anti-keystone pathogen

Abstract: In mammals, a small population of spermatogonial stem cells (SSCs) is established shortly after birth. These cells self-renew and produce sperm for the male’s reproductive lifespan, passing the genome on to the next generation. Establishment of a population of SSCs with high genomic integrity is essential. SSCs are derived from a much larger precursor population of male germ cells (MGCs) that differentiate during fetal life. During the last third of gestation, MGCs undergo a prolonged period of G0 cell cycle arrest during which they sustain high levels of transcription and acquire epigenetic programming for SSC fate. Although these differentiation steps can cause cellular and genomic damage, it has been unclear whether selection for germ cell quality occurs during G0 arrest since no classic markers of cell death have been detected. In this study, we used a mouse model to characterize a population of MGCs that begin to accumulate markers of cell death, such as AnnexinV (AnV) and propidium iodide (PI), at E16.5. The AnV- and PI-positive MGC population is characterized by low expression of the RNA-binding protein, Dead End 1, and exhibits dsDNA breaks and mitochondrial dysfunction. Interestingly, we do not see evidence of an active cell death cascade until the time of birth, when phosphorylation of MLKL, a hallmark of necroptotic cell death, occurs. Based on these findings, we propose that variable cellular health is an important basis for selection of SSC precursors.
Author: Stark, Kara
Source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
Title: In mice, a population of male germ cells show characteristics of nonapoptotic cell death during G0 arrest

Abstract: Background and aims: A variety of self-regulation interventions have shown efficacy in treating Internet Gaming Disorder (IGD), but their shared and unique neurobiological mechanisms remain unclear. This study aims to identify a common, trans-therapeutic neural signature of recovery and to delineate the specific connectivity fingerprints of five different self-regulation interventions for IGD. Methods: This secondary analysis pooled resting-state fMRI data from 269 individuals with IGD who participated in one of five randomized controlled trials of self-regulation-based interventions: Approach Bias Modification (ApBM), Retrieval-Aversive Conditioning (R-AC), Progressive Aerobic Training (PAT), face-to-face Mindfulness Meditation (MM), and a Digital (online) mindfulness intervention. Participants were diagnosed with IGD according to DSM-5. Partial Least Squares (PLS) regression was used to identify a shared connectivity pattern associated with clinical improvement and similarity network fusion to define intervention-specific connectivity fingerprints. Imaging-transcriptomic analysis was further used to explore the molecular correlates. Results: All interventions were associated with significant reductions in IGD severity. PLS analysis identified a shared connectivity pattern predictive of treatment response, characterized by a rebalancing of Subcortical Network (SCN) connectivity along the sensorimotor-association axis. This shared pattern was linked to gene expression profiles related to cellular stress and neuroplasticity. Each intervention also induced a unique connectivity fingerprint, targeting distinct neural circuits. Discussion and Conclusions: Diverse self-regulation interventions for IGD converge on a shared therapeutic pathway involving the large-scale reorganization of cortico-subcortical circuits. These findings identify a robust neurobiological phenotype of recovery, offering a potential biomarker for treatment response and a target for future circuit-based therapies.
Author: Zeng, Ningning
Title: A trans-therapeutic signature of recovery in internet gaming disorder: From shared network reorganization to molecular underpinnings.

Abstract: Abstract We report the first adsorption isotherm of nitrogen dioxide (NO2) in covalent organic frameworks (COFs). Leveraging the dihedral angle (43.6°) of the biphenyl unit in biphenyl-3,3′,5,5′-tetracarbaldehyde, upon reaction with p-phenylenediamine, a three-dimensional COF, PKU-800, has been synthesized. Powder X-ray diffraction, hyperpolarised solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, and modeling collectively reveal that PKU-800 exhibits a triply interpenetrated qtz-type framework structure, which incorporates missing-aldehyde defects (∼8%) and thus pendant amine termini (∼16%). At 298 K, PKU-800 shows remarkable adsorption of NO2 (4.8 and 18.8 mmol g–1 at 0.01 and 1.0 bar, respectively), representing a new benchmark for NO2 sorbents. Dynamic breakthrough experiments confirm efficient capture of NO2 (from 2500 to < 0.1 ppm) by PKU-800 under both dry and wet conditions, with dynamic capacities of 4.97 and 5.27 mmol g–1, respectively. In situ spectroscopic and modeling studies reveal that PKU-800 combines a robust three-dimensional topology, fully accessible channels, and strong binding interactions at both the imine and amino sites to synergistically trap NO2, which can be converted readily to nitric acid upon reaction with water in air.
Author: Thien D. Duong
Source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
Title: Three-Dimensional Covalent Organic Framework for the Capture of Nitrogen Dioxide

Abstract: Abstract Can single-water microsolvation promote proton sharing in a neutral acid–base complex? We address this question for formic acid–ammonia by isolating its monohydrated complex with broadband rotational spectroscopy and interpreting the resolved 14N hyperfine structure with calibrated high-level quantum chemistry. The observed complex is a single dominant HCOOH–NH3–H2O isomer with effective Cs symmetry, in which NH3 remains the primary proton acceptor, while water closes a cooperative hydrogen-bond cycle by accepting from NH3 and donating to the carbonyl oxygen. Rather than simply stabilizing the binary acid–base contact, this water molecule measurably increases its proton-sharing character. A resolved A/E tunneling pattern from NH3 internal rotation supplies the missing orientation needed to rotate the experimental 14N quadrupole tensor into the local ammonia frame, yielding an experimental χzz component and a quadrupole-derived Townes–Dailey ionicity of approximately 26%. High-level structures show the same directional response: O–H elongation, H···N contraction, and O···N contraction relative to HCOOH–NH3. Together, these results show that one water molecule can promote proton sharing in a neutral formic acid–ammonia complex without producing a separated ion pair.
Author: Xie, Fan
Source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
Title: Single-Water Microsolvation Promotes Proton Sharing in a Neutral Formic Acid–Ammonia Complex

Abstract: ABSTRACT Cation pre‐intercalated oxides have been widely explored as cathode materials for aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs). Although the influence of intercalants on the material structure and Zn 2+ storage capacity has been adequately studied, an in‐depth understanding of the influence of intercalants on proton storage is still lacking. Especially, proton transport exhibits ultrafast kinetics as an ideal charge carrier, playing a crucial role in the performance of AZIBs. We show that pre‐intercalated K + in K 0.5 V 6 O 13 (KVO) not only reinforces the [VO] framework but also optimizes the hydrogen‐bonded network composed of confined lattice water, achieving ultrafast proton transport. Benefiting from the optimization of proton topochemistry, the capacity, rate performance, and cycling stability of KVO improve significantly. KVO delivers a high reversible capacity of 462.9 mAh g −1 at 0.2 A g −1 and 82.3% retention after 20000 cycles at 20 A g −1 . Even with the high mass loading of 19.2 mg cm −2 , a KVO||Zn pouch cell with 539.2 mAh capacity can achieve stable cycling for more than 300 cycles at 0.5 A g −1 . This work provides new insights into how pre‐intercalated cations affect the proton topochemistry and electrochemical performance of inorganic cathodes.
Author: Liang, Wenhao
Title: Pre‐Intercalated Cation Optimizing Proton Topochemistry for High‐Performance Aqueous Zinc‐Ion Batteries

Abstract: ABSTRACT The two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e − ORR) for H 2 O 2 production and the subsequent in situ activation to ·OH are constrained by linear scaling relationships, making it difficult for a single active site to simultaneously optimize O 2 activation and H 2 O 2 conversion. This work overcomes the trade‐off by spatially decoupling the cascade reaction onto single‐atom and cluster‐hybrid sites and employing photoelectrocatalysis (PEC). Through a ligand‐exchange and pyrolysis route derived from a metal–organic framework precursor, Bi single atoms and clusters are co‐anchored on B‐doped TiO 2 . The hybrid interface thermodynamically optimizes the intermediate adsorption energies to ensure cascade selectivity, whereas PEC kinetically accelerates the H 2 O 2 ‐to‐·OH conversion by supplying photogenerated electrons. Density functional theory and free‐energy diagrams indicate that H 2 O 2 forms at the single atoms and dissociates into ·OH at the clusters, with the relationship between the p‐band center and ·OH yield following the Sabatier principle. The catalyst delivers a ·OH production rate of 250 µM h −1 at neutral pH and remains active over a broad pH range (3–9). Moreover, it enables broad‐spectrum removal of recalcitrant organic pollutants and retains stable performance over 50 h of operation in a flow‐cell reactor. This work offers guidance for designing cascade catalysts at single‐atom and cluster‐hybrid interfaces.
Author: Wu, Lixu
Subfield: Renewable Energy, Sustainability and the Environment
Title: Spatially Decoupled Cascade Oxygen Reduction on Bi Single‐Atom and Cluster‐Hybrid Sites for Hydroxyl Radical Generation

Abstract: Abstract Understanding how wild populations undergo rapid phenotypic evolution requires linking phenotypic change to its underlying genomic architecture over contemporary timescales. Here, we leverage a 30-year study of Swiss barn owls ( Tyto alba ) to examine long-term changes in two melanin-based traits (plumage coloration and spottiness) that have previously been linked to multiple fitness-related traits. We document a consistent temporal shift toward darker and more heavily spotted individuals and show, using whole-genome sequencing of 3,102 individuals, that these traits are controlled by a small number of loci of major effect with partially overlapping architectures. Temporal allele frequency analyses reveal subtle but consistent changes at these loci. By comparing empirical trajectories to simulations, we show that genetic drift alone is insufficient to explain the observed patterns at one major locus, indicating a role for selection. Our results demonstrate how selection acting on a small number of loci can contribute to rapid phenotypic evolution of continuous traits in the wild and highlight the value of long-term genomic and phenotypic monitoring for disentangling evolutionary processes.
Author: Cumer, Tristan
Title: Genomic bases of short-term evolution in wild barn owls revealed by long-term monitoring and population-scale sequencing

Abstract: A systematic molecular dynamics study of sulfur dioxide (SO2) and methane (CH4) incorporation in 24 imidazolium-based ionic liquids is presented, spanning different anion families and cation alkyl chain lengths. The two gases represent limiting cases of solvation behavior in ionic liquids: SO2 exhibits strong electrostatic interactions and Lewis amphoteric character, whereas CH4 is governed primarily by weak London dispersion forces. Radial distribution functions, coordination numbers, cluster-size distributions, and interaction energies were analyzed to elucidate the molecular organization of the mixtures. The results show that neither SO2 nor CH4 substantially disrupts the polar network of the ionic liquids. SO2 partitions between the polar and nonpolar regions of the ionic liquid, leading to reduced self-association and more gas distributions, whereas CH4 preferentially occupies alkyl-rich regions and exhibits only weak self-association with minimal dependence on cation chain length. Interaction energy decomposition highlights the dominant role of electrostatics in SO2 solvation and the free volume-driven, weakly interacting nature of CH4 incorporation. These findings provide a molecular-level framework for rationalizing incorporation trends and for guiding the design of ionic liquids for gas separation, highlighting how polarity, anion charge distribution, and cation alkyl chain length can be tuned to enhance specific SO2 stabilization while controlling nonspecific CH4 accommodation in alkyl-rich free-volume domains.
Author: Marques, Hugo
Title: Structural and energetic signatures of SO2 and CH4 incorporation in imidazolium-based ionic liquids

Abstract: Controversial celebrities are the wrong spokespeople for a healthier America, writes Sophie Harman
Author: Harman, Sophie
Title: MAHA Summit platformed controversial celebrities and forgot its political base

Abstract: Background Kidney transplant care in low-resource countries is often affected by multiple factors, including workforce constraints, fragmented communication, and medication access challenges. Given pharmacists’ involvement in medication management and regular patient follow-up, this study was designed to explore transplant care delivery in Iraq from pharmacists’ perspectives. Method Qualitative data were collected using face-to-face, semi-structured interviews with all eligible pharmacists from the two major governmental hospitals in Baghdad caring for kidney transplant recipients. Afterwards, data were analyzed using Braun and Clarke’s reflexive thematic analysis approach. Results This study included 13 pharmacists, 5 of whom were working in the clinical transplant wards, whereas the remaining 8 were working in the outpatient consultation setting. Four descriptive themes were identified: Dispensing-centered practice within a constrained and evolving pharmacist role, fragmented yet adaptive interprofessional collaboration, patient education as an informal and inconsistently delivered practice, and medication availability within a constrained and variably regulated supply system. Conclusion This study highlights the adaptive approaches used by pharmacists in an attempt to maintain medication access and patient support with the available resources. However, the study findings also highlight challenges that extend beyond the capacity of individual pharmacists to resolve and suggest the need for more structured organizational support, clearer communication pathways, and an integrated system to strengthen Iraqi transplant care practices within comparable governmental settings.
Author: Sarah M Faisal
Title: Barriers and enablers shaping kidney transplant care delivery: Insights from Iraqi pharmacists

Abstract: Missing data is a challenging issue in data analysis. Researchers often address the issue by simply removing incomplete cases from the analysis. However, this approach reduces the sample size and can undermine the accuracy of statistical estimates. Alternatively, imputation techniques can be used to replace missing values with plausible estimates, resulting in a more complete dataset and more reliable estimates. In this study, we propose a new imputation method, which we call Layered Stacking. The method is designed to improve the estimation of continuous missing values. To evaluate its effectiveness, comprehensive simulation studies were carried out with four distinct data generating processes using datasets generated under the missing at random mechanism, with sample sizes of 500, 1,000, 5,000 and 10,000, and missingness rates of 10, 20, 30 and 40%. The proposed method is compared with five widely used imputation techniques: k-nearest neighbors, support vector regression, decision tree, random forest and extreme gradient boosting. Evaluation metrics include mean squared imputation error (MSIE) and mean absolute percentage imputation error (MAPIE) along with standard deviation (SD) and 95% confidence interval (CI) across replications. Two real-world datasets have also been considered to assess the performance of the method. The proposed method generally achieved lower MSIE than the benchmark models, particularly for larger datasets.
Author: Asif, Muhammad
Title: A layered stacking ensemble approach for missing data imputation

Abstract: Quiet quitting has emerged as a contemporary work behavior associated with reduced organizational engagement and increased work-related stress, particularly among healthcare professionals. This study aimed to adapt the Quiet Quitting Scale into Turkish and evaluate its validity and reliability among healthcare workers. This methodological study was conducted online between February and April 2025. The sample included 298 healthcare professionals currently working in Turkey. Data were collected using the “Personal Information Form” and the “Quiet Quitting Scale.” Content validity analysis showed item-level I-CVI values ranging from 0.83 to 1.00, with a total scale S-CVI of 0.97. Factor loadings for individual items ranged from 0.510 to 0.890. Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) confirmed that the proposed factor structure fitted the data well, with model fit indices as follows: χ² = 64.31; df = 21; p < 0.05; χ²/df = 3.06; RMSEA = 0.083; CFI = 0.97; SRMR = 0.052; TLI = 0.95; RMR = 0.069; AIC = 112.31. These findings provide strong support for the structural validity of the scale. The Turkish version of the Quiet Quitting Scale demonstrates both validity and reliability, making it a suitable tool for evaluating quiet quitting tendencies among healthcare workers.
Author: Kurt, Nuray
Subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management
Title: Adaptation of the Quiet Quitting Scale into Turkish: A methodological study

Abstract: We develop a complete-market production economy in which heterogeneous beliefs about productivity growth affect both asset prices and real activity. Firms must hire workers before productivity is realized, so operating leverage increases the exposure of profits to productivity risk. Because the firm’s discount factor depends on a wealth-weighted aggregation of investor beliefs, shifts in optimism compress risk premia and raise employment, while reversals trigger contractions. This mechanism generates an equilibrium feedback between asset prices, hiring, and risk exposure. A taxonomy of belief systems shows that only extrapolative beliefs produce amplification and endogenous risk build-up. Disciplined by survey expectations, the model jointly matches key asset-pricing, trading-volume, and business-cycle moments.
Author: Bigio, Saki
Title: Heterogeneous beliefs, asset prices, and business cycles

Abstract: Abstract Autistic children and adolescents exhibit alterations in multisensory processing of simple audiovisual stimuli and complex speech stimuli. Multisensory perceptual training improves audiovisual simultaneity perception in typically developed adults, thereby facilitating speech comprehension in noise. We hypothesized that multisensory training would enhance audiovisual integration and speech comprehension in noise in autistic youth. A brief simultaneity judgment task (SJT) with feedback as the training paradigm was administered to a sample of autistic participants (aged 8–17). Simple audiovisual integration and speech comprehension were assessed before training (T0), immediately (T1), seven (T2) and 14 days (T3) after training. For simple audiovisual stimuli, changes in simultaneity judgements were observed at T1 and T2. At T1, these changes may reflect a shift in response criteria, whereas at T2, a narrower TBW and a steeper slope may indicate improved simultaneity perception. In a Word Recognition Task (WRT), no significant improvements were observed. This study suggests that multisensory training alters simultaneity judgement in a SJT in autistic youth, with the effects persisting seven days. Future studies should determine whether these effects reflect changes in response criteria or genuine improvements in simultaneity perception and determine how training paradigms must be adapted to enhance speech comprehension in autistic youth.
Author: Möde, Laura
Title: Multimodal speech perception in noise after multisensory perceptual training in autistic children and adolescents

Abstract: Abstract Depression affects younger populations, while imbalanced diet may contribute to disease development, with myelin abnormalities representing one possible underlying mechanism. We previously showed that maternal high-fat diet (HFD; 60% energy from fat) during pregnancy and lactation induces depressive-like behavior and myelin-related alterations in the prefrontal cortex (PFC) of rat offspring. We investigated whether post-weaning docosahexaenoic acid (DHA)- or eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA)-enriched diets until adulthood could reverse these abnormalities. Depressive-like behavior was assessed in the forced swimming test (FST), while myelin-related changes were analyzed using RT-qPCR, ELISA, and immunofluorescence staining. Both DHA and EPA-enriched diets normalized increased immobility time in adult offspring. In male offspring, both diets normalized the mRNA levels of genes encoding myelin-oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (MOG), 2′,3′-cyclic nucleotide 3′-phosphodiesterase (CNPase), and transferrin, whereas only EPA additionally restored the mRNA levels of genes encoding myelin and lymphocyte protein (MAL) and kallikrein 6 (KLK6). At the protein level, DHA normalized only MOG, while EPA restored MOG, MAL, and CNPase levels. In females, both DHA and EPA increased Mog mRNA levels, whereas DHA additionally increased Klk6 mRNA expression compared to offspring exposed to maternal HFD and post-weaning SD. At the cellular level, DHA and EPA produced sex-specific effects, with broader restoration of oligodendrocytes and myelin intensity in males. Maternal HFD also decreased brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) levels in male offspring (mRNA and protein level), while post-weaning DHA and EPA supplementation restored Bdnf mRNA expression. Overall, post-weaning DHA and EPA alleviated maternal HFD-induced FST-assessed depressive-like behavior and partially restored myelin-related abnormalities in the PFC, with EPA exerting broader molecular and cellular effects than DHA.
Author: Śliwa, Maya
Title: Post-weaning DHA or EPA supplementation attenuates depressive-like behavior and myelination deficits induced by maternal high-fat diet in rat offspring

Abstract: The human transmembrane protein SERINC5 incorporates into budding HIV-1 particles and inhibits virus fusion with target cells. Although three other human SERINC paralogs display antiviral activity, their contribution to retroviral restriction and their susceptibility to viral antagonists have not been systematically compared. HIV-1 Nef, Moloney murine leukemia virus (MoMLV) glycoGag, and the equine infectious anemia virus (EIAV) S2 glycoprotein independently evolved mechanisms to counteract SERINC5. Here, we show that all human SERINC paralogs are incorporated into HIV-1 virions despite their differing antiviral activities. However, compared with the other SERINC paralogs, SERINC5 is selectively and efficiently targeted by all retroviral antagonists examined, supporting the notion that SERINC5 has exerted the strongest selective pressure on retroviral evolution. We identified a tri-cysteine motif within intracellular loop 4 (ICL4) as a critical determinant of SERINC5 antagonism by Nef. Disruption of this motif impaired Nef-mediated internalization, exclusion from virions, and full rescue of HIV-1 infectivity by diverse HIV-1 and SIV Nef alleles, but had no effect on antagonism by MoMLV glycoGag or EIAV S2, indicating that these viral proteins recognize distinct molecular features of SERINC5. Transfer of ICL4 to SERINC2 was insufficient to confer Nef sensitivity, demonstrating that the tri-cysteine motif is necessary but not sufficient for antagonism. Finally, we show that this motif is palmitoylated, suggesting that palmitoylation contributes to SERINC5 recognition by Nef. Together, these findings establish SERINC5 as the principal target of retroviral antagonists and demonstrate that its recognition by Nef depends on the broader structural context of SERINC5. IMPORTANCE: The SERINC family of multipass transmembrane proteins includes host factors capable of restricting retrovirus infectivity. Among the five human paralogs, SERINC5 displays the strongest antiviral activity and is the only member efficiently targeted by all known retroviral antagonists, including HIV-1 Nef, MLV glycoGag, and the EIAV S2. This selectivity indicates that the evolutionary pressure exerted by SERINC proteins on retroviruses has been primarily driven by SERINC5 rather than by its relatives. Through structure-guided mutagenesis, we identified a tri-cysteine motif within intracellular loop 4 as a crucial determinant for SERINC5 downregulation by Nef, providing a molecular explanation for its distinctive susceptibility. These findings establish SERINC5 as the principal target of viral counteraction and suggest that its molecular features have contributed to shaping the adaptation of primate lentiviral Nef proteins to the host.
Author: Bertelli, Cinzia
Title: SERINC5 is the primary target of retroviral antagonists among human SERINC paralogs and requires a tri-cysteine motif for its counteraction by HIV-1 Nef

Abstract: Humans struggle to produce random behavior when asked to do so, leading some to suggest that our ability to randomize is attenuated (or even absent). Here, we demonstrate that the capacity for random behavior is much greater than previously acknowledged: Humans can behave in (near) optimally random ways when the context demands it. We created a custom, online version of the game Battleship in which participants competed against one another. On each turn, one player chose a tile on a 3 × 3 grid to place a ship, while the other player tried to guess the ship's location. Across six preregistered studies, this strategic context led to dramatic increases in random behavior relative to closely matched non-strategic tasks. Such random behavior was also remarkably flexible and optimal depending on context; both players readily incorporated varying information about the game (e.g., that tiles can differ in value) while simultaneously accounting for their opponents' knowledge of that information. A computational model validated these findings and revealed nuanced differences across contexts. Contrary to decades of work finding that humans fail to randomize, we find that strategic games promote highly flexible, near-random behavior.
Author: Boger, Tal
Title: Near-random behavior in strategic games

Abstract: Oral diseases in later life reflect cumulative biological, social, and health-system exposures. This documentary, descriptive, comparative secondary analysis used published aggregate estimates from SB Brasil 2010 and SB Brasil 2023, two nationwide cross-sectional oral-health surveys conducted by the Brazilian Ministry of Health. Official survey reports were the quantitative data sources, while a structured narrative review of PubMed, SciELO, LILACS, and Ministry of Health documents was used only for contextual interpretation. Published estimates for adults aged 65–74 years were extracted and harmonized across survey editions and compared descriptively using means, percentages, absolute and relative changes, territorial ranges, and, where available in the official reports, 95% confidence intervals; no individual-level records or statistically pooled study-level effect estimates were analyzed. The national mean DMFT declined from 27.53 in 2010 to 23.55 in 2023. At the national level, the mean missing-teeth component declined from 25.29 (91.9% of DMFT) to 19.86 (84.32%), whereas the restored-without-caries component increased from 1.62 to 2.78. Poor self-perceived oral health declined from 25.2% to 10.9%, while positive ratings remained nearly unchanged (52.6% vs. 52.7%). In 2023, untreated caries ranged from 44.27% in Maranhão (95% CI 34.85–53.70) to 19.07% in Santa Catarina (95% CI 12.00–26.14). These findings document temporal improvement together with geographic heterogeneity. Structural-vulnerability mechanisms and implications for underserved populations are interpreted from the previous literature and were not directly tested in the present aggregate analysis.
Author: Geanny Carolline Pereira Leão
Source: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
Title: Oral Health Trends and Territorial Inequalities Among Older Adults in Brazil: Comparative Secondary Analysis of SB Brasil 2010 and 2023

Abstract: Abstract Adiponectin is a fat-derived adipocytokine that has been associated with laminitis risk in ponies. Factors that affect sampling timing for measurement of adiponectin concentration have been inadequately investigated. This study aimed to determine the effect of an oral glucose test (OGT) and fed-state on adiponectin concentration in horses and ponies. Blood samples were collected before and after an OGT in 85 horses and ponies and high molecular weight (HMW) adiponectin concentration was measured. Total adiponectin concentration was measured in a subset of 25 animals. Assays validated for use with horse plasma were used. Next, HMW adiponectin was measured before and for up to 4 hours after the consumption of three different diets in ponies: pasture (n = 16), a soyabean meal diet (n = 10) or diet with added maize and molasses (n = 5). The groups were compared with a Kruskal Wallis rank sum test, with Dunn’s post-hoc test, and timepoints with a signed-rank, or Pearson’s, test. The ratios were compared with a paired t-test. Stepwise rank-based regression was used to consider multiple predictors for the change in HMW adiponectin concentration during the OGT. Friedman’s test was used to examine changes in concentration over time after meal consumption. Both the OGT and the diet containing maize caused a larger (P < 0.05) change in blood glucose concentration (0h to 2h) than the pasture or diet with soyabean meal. The OGT meal increased (P < 0.001) median [IQR] post-prandial HMW adiponectin concentration at the 2 h timepoint (4.02 [2.23—6.88] µg/mL), compared to the pre-test sample (2.75 [1.17—5.69] µg/mL). However, median [IQR] total adiponectin concentration did not change from the 0 h (7.78 [4.19—12.7] µg/mL) to the 2 h sample (6.48 [4.04—12.8] µg/mL). The proportion of HMW multimers in the total adiponectin concentration increased (P = 0.01) from 37% to 54% post-prandially. Pasture grazing and consumption of a soyabean or maize based meal did not result in a change in HMW adiponectin concentration over time. Blood samples for the measurement of HMW adiponectin should be taken before animals receive an in-feed OGT.
Author: Melody Anne de Laat
Title: An in-feed oral glucose test increases post-prandial high molecular weight adiponectin concentration in horses

Abstract: This paper examines how police interviewers use references to non-present third parties as interactional resources for accomplishing institutional goals in interviews with suspects. Drawing on 24 police interviews analysed using conversation analysis, the study focuses on sequences in which detectives pursue admissions or other case-relevant actions. The analysis identifies four recurrent practices accomplished through third-party references: testing the veracity of accounts, establishing relational links as preliminary, challenging accounts through third-party statements and invoking moral accountability. These practices involve turns which are formatted as information-seeking or knowledge-claiming moves, while simultaneously projecting institutionally consequential implications. The findings highlight the central role of the epistemic and moral domains in shaping action formation and institutional trajectories in police interviews.
Author: Cerović, Marijana
Title: Third-party mentions and action forwarding in police interviews
